pages.title: Rooted in this place.
pages.label: About the museum
pages.intro: The museum shares the history of South Central Oklahoma through artifacts collected from around the area, from an early electric car to one of the earliest examples of a steam-pumper fire engine.

sections.title: Our largest artifact is the building itself
sections.text: Built in 1935–1936 by the Works Progress Administration, this limestone armory originally served the local National Guard. Today, its walls hold the stories of our region.

sections.title: Our mission
sections.text: To collect, preserve and interpret the social, cultural and economic history of South Central Oklahoma with a special emphasis on Ardmore and Carter County.

sections.title: Many stories under one roof
sections.text: Major exhibits are housed in three main wings. The north wing’s Transportation and Industry Gallery explores railroads, cotton and oil, with early carriages, saddles, soapbox derby cars and a working model of oil-field equipment. The south wing includes From the Ashes, the Fonville Gallery, the Genealogical Library and items found in early homes of the area. Ardmore’s first steam-powered fire engine is among its highlights.

sections.title: Tools of Our Land
sections.text: Completed in May 2017, two 5,000-square-foot buildings explore the farming and ranching history of the area.

sections.title: Honoring those who served
sections.text: The Military Memorial Museum preserves military history from the American Revolution to the Gulf Wars and honors our nation’s veterans. Its displays include everyday items used by soldiers, models and uniforms representing all eight uniformed services.

pages.title: Honoring those who served.
pages.label: Military Memorial Museum
pages.intro: Preserving military history and honoring the people of all service branches who have served this country in war and peace.

sections.title: History
sections.text: The Military Memorial Museum is housed in the west wing of the building that once served as a National Guard Armory for Oklahoma’s historic, battle-proven 45th Division. Built by the Works Progress Administration in 1935–1936, the building itself is a monument to that period in Oklahoma’s and the nation’s history. The men and women who serve as guides, or “Charge of Quarters,” are volunteers.

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text: Displays in the museum represent all eras: the Civil War, the Spanish-American War, the Indian Wars, World War I, World War II, the Korean Conflict, Vietnam, the Gulf War and the Iraqi Freedom War. The displays include artifacts, documents, photographs, uniforms, weapons, knives, models, medals and a great deal of personal memorabilia from veterans all over the United States.

sections.title: Mission
sections.text: Our mission from the beginning has been to preserve and display military history, and to honor those persons of all service branches who have served this country in war and peace.

sections.title: Funding
sections.text: Although the Military Memorial Museum is located in the Greater Southwest Historical Museum, it is self-supporting and does not share in the gifts or donations made to the larger museum. Memberships and Hall of Honor donations are important sources of support.

sections.title: Hall of Honor
sections.text: A donation of $50 purchases an engraved plate showing the donor’s name and the name of the recipient being honored. Memorials may be made “In Memory Of” a veteran family member or veteran friend from any state or branch of service. The entrance and main corridor of the Military Memorial Museum are recognized as the Hall of Honor.

sections.title: Ardmore Army Air Field history
sections.text: Explore the history of Ardmore Army Air Field (1942–1946) and Ardmore Air Force Base (1953–1959). This memorial website is dedicated to the men and women who served with distinction at Ardmore Army Air Field, a training base for the U.S. Army Air Forces.

pages.title: A little holiday wonder.
pages.label: Santa’s House on the Prairie
pages.intro: Santa’s House on the Prairie is an event designed for schoolchildren ages three to seven years old. Participating children enjoy decorating ornaments, exploring our Holiday Forest, and listening to stories read by Mr. and Mrs. Claus.

sections.title: A memorable morning
sections.text: Begin in the Holiday Forest, enjoy stories with Mr. and Mrs. Claus, decorate an ornament and receive cookies. Allow about 30 minutes for the activities.

sections.title: Plan your group’s visit
sections.text: The program takes place during the first two weeks of December. Please call between August and October to schedule. Appointments are offered at 15-minute intervals from 9 to 11:30 a.m. The listed cost is $2 per child; confirm current availability and pricing when booking. Spaces fill quickly, so please reserve early.

sections.title: Help make the magic
sections.text: Volunteers help keep the program running throughout its two-week season. Roles include movie attendant, playing Mr. or Mrs. Claus, group attendant and crafting assistant. Contact Cassandra, our curator, by email or call the museum to volunteer.

sections.title: Sponsor a Holiday Forest tree
sections.text: Tree sponsorship helps offset program costs. Sponsors’ names are displayed on the trees. The existing program lists a display period from the beginning of November through January 1; confirm this season’s dates with the curator. Small and large trees are available. Decorate your own tree or ask staff to decorate it for an additional fee; staff will do their best to use your chosen colors or theme. Contact Cassandra for current prices.

Call ahead for group programs or a research appointment rather than relying on general museum hours.

sections.title: Hours and admission
sections.text: Free admission. Tuesday–Saturday · 10 a.m.–5 p.m.. Closed Sundays, Mondays and holidays. Call 580-226-3857 before traveling for a holiday visit, group program or special appointment. The museum is in Ardmore, not in Tishomingo.

sections.title: Planning for your group
sections.text: Tell the museum about your group size, interests and any access needs before your trip. Group reservations need at least one week’s notice. Genealogical research has separate hours, and seasonal programs require their own booking arrangements.
